title: A-1000 assembly & design review
registerRevision: 2026-09-10 · Physical equipment ownership and complete Explore assemblies
lead: Wastewater treatment: equalization T-1006, neutralization / precipitation / polishing / flocculation reactors R-1001 … R-1004, decanter centrifuge DC-1001, reagent storage and dosing (NaOH, lime, BaCl₂, HCl, floc aid: T-1001 … T-1005 with P-1001 … P-1004 and M-1001), transfer pumps P-1005 … P-1010, the model-side Pre-G decant sump T-1007 / P-1011, centrate receiver T-1008 / P-1012, sludge bin BIN-1001 and control station CP-1001, with twelve bunds, three fire points and seven emergency stations.

findings.topic: Discharge route and acid recovery — the governing decision
findings.status: Design lever identified — no flow approved
findings.reason: The wastewater flow, its acid load and therefore every reactor, reagent and sludge quantity depend on whether spent acid is recovered before A-1000.
findings.observation: D-A1000-01 approves the REP-038 first-principles load as the design statement — 0.64 mol/L H₂SO₄ + 0.23 mol/L HCl (179 t/d H₂SO₄, 24 t/d HCl, 129 kmol/d H₃PO₄) with Mn / K / P: the feed is dilute acid, not wastewater — and REP-039's acid recovery (150–200 t/d spent-acid reconcentration, 1.5–4.4 MW at 150–200 °C) as the governing design lever. No flow is approved: 2,850 m³/d as drawn, 400–600 m³/d with acid recovery, or the DBM 30–75 m³/d corrected by MOC-001 to a range by case. No A-1000 stream table exists; the model volumes (T-1006 200 m³, R-1001 35 m³, R-1002 65 m³, R-1003 / R-1004 45 m³) are screening allowances.
findings.action: Decide the A-1000 discharge route and the spent-acid recovery case (REP-039; MOC-001 Part D.1) before any A-1000 / A-2000 sizing; then issue the first A-1000 / A-2000 stream tables on DBM V2.0 with the wastewater range by case (REP-038).

findings.topic: Treatment chemistry — NaOH stage not viable, lime-first flowsheet
findings.status: Intent adopted — MoC on PFD-1000 required
findings.reason: At 0.64 mol/L the drawn rapid NaOH neutralisation would consume ≈ 166 t/d NaOH and leave sulphate soluble, making downstream RO unworkable.
findings.observation: D-A1000-02 adopts REP-038: the NaOH "rapid" stage to pH 3–4 is not viable (≈ 166 t/d NaOH, ≈ $22 M/y; sulphate stays soluble; Na₂SO₄ at 61 g/L makes RO unworkable) — lime-first flowsheet adopted as intent, with R-1001's duty to be redefined; the lime stage to pH 8.5–10.5 at ≈ 149 t/d Ca(OH)₂ producing ≈ 314 t/d gypsum + 20 t/d Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 5 t/d Mn sludge (Case 0) as the chemistry basis; BaCl₂ polishing (R-1003) conditional on the local sewer sulphate limit vs gypsum saturation (≈ 1,480 mg/L). The ≈ 2 MW neutralisation heat and the ≈ 340 t/d sludge rate are withdrawn as case-dependent. The model still carries the NaOH tank T-1001 and dosing pump P-1004 as drawn.
findings.action: Raise the MoC on FEED-PFD-1000: remove the NaOH rapid-neutralisation stage or re-purpose R-1001 (lime / limestone-then-lime high-density sludge); restate T-1001 / T-1002 and the dosing pumps; fix the sulphate limit with the receiving authority.

findings.reason: Gypsum-dominated sludge at hundreds of tonnes per day decides the decanter, the bin and the truck movements; all follow the acid-recovery case.
findings.observation: D-A1000-02 withdrew the DC-1001 feed basis (≈ 340 t/d sludge in Case 0). The model provides the decanter with feed pump P-1009 and a conditional bypass pump P-1010, a covered sludge bin BIN-1001 whose classification is pending, an 8 m³ centrate receiver T-1008 with transfer / recycle pump P-1012, and the Pre-G gravity-decant sump T-1007 / P-1011 — the last five are model-only tags without register identity.
findings.action: Size DC-1001, BIN-1001 and the sludge handling on the chosen case; classify the sludge (gypsum with Mn / P) for disposal; register the model-only tags or record them by decision.

findings.status: Ruled — M-1001 and T-1005 not yet covered
findings.reason: Dilute mixed acid, lime slurry, BaCl₂, HCl and gypsum slurry each set their own wetted materials.
findings.observation: D-A1000-MOC applies MAT-002 to sixteen items: dual-laminate FRP / HDPE / rubber-lined carbon steel for the acid-side tanks and reactors (T-1006, R-1001 … R-1004), HDPE or rubber-lined carbon steel for lime storage (T-1002), and the matching pump and centrifuge selections; MDL-001 (XLPE / HDPE, rubber-lined CS) superseded. M-1001 and T-1005 (floc aid) keep an MDL-001 material only.
findings.action: Extend MAT-002 to M-1001 and T-1005; issue datasheets once the flowsheet (A1000-02) and the case (A1000-01) are fixed.

findings.reason: A reagent farm with NaOH, lime, BaCl₂, HCl and 200 m³ of acidic equalization needs retention, access and emergency provision sized to the real inventories.
findings.observation: The model owns twelve bunds (from 4.6 m³ under floc-aid storage to 265 m³ under the equalization tank — all retention figures scale from screening volumes), the access / containment structure PL-1001, control station CP-1001, three fire points and seven emergency stations, none on LST-001. The inbound streams from A-300 (acidic centrate) and A-400 (wash water) are model interfaces without a stated flow; the A-160 wastewater and decant interfaces have no A-1000 destination.
findings.action: Re-derive retention from the case-based inventories; assign the inbound interface flows in the stream tables; register bunds, stations, fire points and PL-1001 / CP-1001 or record them by decision.

findings.topic: Acid route decided (D-A1000-03): spent-acid recovery, REP-039 Route 2 + 6
findings.status: Base case approved — gated on M1–M3; A-1000 to be sized for the residual
findings.reason: D-A1000-01 left A-1000 unfrozen until the acid-recovery decision: recovery removes ≈ 95 % of the A-1000 load and sets its size, reagents and sludge.
findings.observation: D-A1000-03 makes spent-acid recovery (REP-039 Route 2 + 6) the FEED base case for the wet train: TLGO is separated from 50–60 wt % acid in A-300 (Route 2) and the GIC from the A-160 acid before washing (Route 6); the filtrates are reconcentrated and recycled, leaving A-1000 the residual (≈ 6–15 t/d acid, gypsum ≈ 10–25 t/d instead of ≈ 314 t/d). The route is gated on M1 (filterability at 50–60 wt %), M2 (recycled-acid quality) and M3 (Mn(VII) = 0 before heating); Route 0 (neutralise everything in A-1000) stays as the fallback envelope. The first rework is issued: A-300 moves to a 55 wt % endpoint with its filtrate to the concentrator (FEED-PE-CAL-032 V1.1, D-A300-06). The A-1000 feed, duty and sludge bases stay unapproved (D-A1000-01 / -02) until the residual is sized.
findings.action: Revise A-160 for Route 6 (CAL-016, T-161 / T-162 / F-161); draft the spent-acid concentrator package (≈ 135 + 36 t/d, A-5400 duty); then size A-1000 for the residual with the Route 0 envelope noted; run M1–M3.

findings.topic: Spent-acid concentrator package (D-A1000-04): new area A-1100 — PK-1101, T-1101, T-1102, P-1101A/B, P-1102A/B
findings.status: Budget envelope issued — design concept approved; gated on the M5 vendor enquiry, heat supply on MOC-002 Part F
findings.reason: Route 2 + 6 (D-A1000-03) sends the A-300 filtrate and the A-160 acid to recovery instead of A-1000; the plant needs the concentrator that closes the loop, and its heat and vent loads land on A-5400 and A-3000.
findings.observation: D-A1000-04 carries the concentrator on bases CN1–CN9 approved by QFL 2026-09-26, as FEED-PE-CAL-033 and FEED-PE-DAT-109…113 (register V7.4) in a new area A-1100 (REP-039 §9), recorded in the A-1000 data layer until the model has that area. Feed on the current basis: 170 t/d of A-300 filtrate at 55 wt % and 26.9 t/d of A-160 acid at 90 wt % — 117.6 t/d H₂SO₄ (REP-039 quoted 135–175 t/d on the older basis), with ≈ 9.7 t/d H₃PO₄ and 5.8 t/d Mn / K salts. PK-1101, a two-stage vacuum package (55 → ≈ 75 wt %, MVR option; 75 → 93 wt % at 150–180 °C, 50–100 mbar), is rated 140 t/d and returns ≈ 134 t/d of 93 wt % acid with its H₃PO₄ — 115.5 t/d H₂SO₄ recovered after the salt-cake loss — so purchased acid falls from ≈ 135 to ≈ 18 t/d. It evaporates ≈ 55 t/d of water: 2.26 MW normal, 2.69 MW rated, 3.5 MW design on A-5400 (1.66 GJ / t), condensers 2.0 MW on A-5200; the MVR option ≈ 0.9 MW thermal plus 0.8–1.2 MW electrical. T-1101 (100 m³ FRP) holds two A-300 batches and one A-160 batch behind the Mn(VII) = 0 ORP interlock; T-1102 (200 m³ carbon steel) holds two days of product for the M2 quality release — CN9’s 150 m³ did not hold two days, and P-1101 went from 6 to 7 m³/h to cover the rated feed. Budget ≈ $15–30 M. Heat above 95 °C is not shown as served until MOC-002 Part F; the A-5400 screen rises to ≈ 17.6–21.8 MW against the 10 MW provision.
findings.action: Issue the M5 vendor enquiry (stage split, MVR, materials, footprint, CAPEX); resolve the A-5400 heat supply in MOC-002 Part F; check the A-3000 S1 load for the concentrator vent (SO₂ / CO₂); classify the salt cake; run M2 on reconcentrated filtrate; add A-1100 to the PFD, LST-001, MAT-002 and the model; then size A-1000 for the residual.

findings.topic: A-1000 sized for the Route 2 + 6 residual (D-A1000-05): lime-only HDS — phase 1 datasheets; NaOH and Pre-G decant items retired
findings.status: Feed, solids and duty bases approved; phase 1 datasheets issued as candidates; sewer limit, HCl dose and A-400 flows held
findings.reason: D-A1000-01 left A-1000 unfrozen until the acid route was decided; with D-A1000-03 / -04 the load is the residual, 5–10 × smaller than the as-drawn 2,850 m³/d and 179 t/d.
findings.observation: D-A1000-05 on bases RS1–RS9 approved by QFL 2026-09-27 (FEED-PE-CAL-034, FEED-PE-DAT-114…122, register V7.7). The residual on the current basis: A-160 T-163 32 m³/d with 2.3 t/d H₂SO₄; the A-300 cake liquor 14.2 t/d H₂SO₄ through A-300 phase 2 / A-400 (the largest load, 60–75 %); the A-1100 salt-cake liquor 2.1 t/d; a 5.8 t/d organics-bleed allowance (M2) — 18.6 t/d firm, 24.3 t/d design, against REP-039 / REP-038’s 6–15 t/d. HCl from A-300 phase 2 is 3 t/d at the M3 estimate and 18.2 t/d at the PFD dose; reagent systems are sized for the bounding dose. Flow 495 m³/d normal, 615 m³/d design (25.6 m³/h). Lime-only HDS: Ca(OH)₂ 20.7–40.5 t/d, gypsum 35.8–45.6 t/d (REP-038 Case 4: 10–25), 52 t/d dry solids, 0.34 MW absorbed (no cooler). T-1006 400 m³ (12 h), R-1001 25 m³ (pH 5–6, 45 min), R-1002 30 m³ (pH 9.8–10, 40 min with 30 % recycle), R-1004 10 m³, new thickener CL-1001 Ø 6.5 m (RS5 quoted Ø 6 m; the solids need 29 m²), DC-1001 8 m³/h → 87 t/d cake, T-1002 an 80 m³ lime slurry day tank fed from a hydrated-lime silo (two days of slurry would have been ≈ 410 m³), P-1003A/B 10 m³/h ring main, P-1005A/B 30 m³/h. The CAL-034 feed, solids and duty rows close the three properties D-A1000-01 / -02 left unapproved; T-1001 / P-1004 (NaOH) and T-1007 / P-1011 (Pre-G decant) are recorded as retired; 24 missing-value gaps close.
findings.action: Settle the sewer sulphate limit (BaCl₂ stage R-1003 held); re-derive the A-300 phase 2 HCl dose (REP-037 M3) and consider a C-301 cake wash to send the cake liquor to the concentrator instead; confirm the A-400 flows (hold H-01); run settling / dewatering tests; classify the sludge; raise the PFD-1000 MoC (CL-1001, lime silo, NaOH deleted); remove the retired tags from the model; issue the phase 2 datasheets.

findings.topic: A-300 cake wash (D-A300-07): A-1100 revised to V1.1; A-1000 residual falls, not re-balanced
findings.status: A-1100 V1.1 issued as candidates; A-1000 sizes kept as margin (basis CW8)
findings.reason: Moving the A-300 cake-liquor acid to the concentrator changes both the A-1100 load and the A-1000 residual carried in A1000-07 / A1000-08.
findings.observation: A-1100 (basis CW7): FEED-PE-CAL-033 and FEED-PE-DAT-109…113 V1.1 (register V8.6) — 132.3 t/d H₂SO₄ to PK-1101 (was 117.6), 129.8 t/d recovered, 62.8 t/d water evaporated, 2.59 MW normal and 2.93 MW at the new 150 t/d rating (was 140) — the 3.5 MW design still covers rated × 1.1, but the 150 t/d rating leaves 13 % over normal, not 15 %; T-1101 100 → 125 m³ (two A-300 batches are now 89 m³), P-1101 7 → 8 m³/h, T-1102 two-day volume 165 m³ in 200 m³. A-1000 (basis CW8): the residual H₂SO₄ falls from 24.3 to ≈ 10.8 t/d design (18.6 → ≈ 5.1 firm), lime from 40.5 to ≈ 30 t/d, gypsum from 45.6 to ≈ 22 t/d; FEED-PE-CAL-034 and DAT-114…122 are not revised — the spare capacity is margin for the unresolved A-300 phase 2 HCl dose (M3) and organics bleed (M2), to be re-balanced at phase 2. The data layer reads the A-1100 V1.0 sheets from the archive and lets V1.1 supersede them in full; no existing valueId changed.
findings.action: Re-balance CAL-034 when M2 / M3 are settled (phase 2), and consider a 160 t/d PK-1101 rating in the vendor enquiry (M5) to restore a 15 % margin.

findings.topic: A-1000 phase 2 (D-A1000-06): gravity cascade, solids handling, lime silo, polymer; BaCl₂ stage priced as an option; six more tags retired
findings.status: Retirements approved; phase 2 datasheets issued as candidates; BaCl₂ built only if the permit requires it
findings.reason: The phase 1 HDS flowsheet (A1000-08) left the solids handling, reagents and the conditional sulphate stage unsized, and made several register items redundant.
findings.observation: D-A1000-06 on bases P2-1–P2-9 approved by QFL 2026-09-27 (FEED-PE-CAL-035, FEED-PE-DAT-123…131, register V8.9), sized on the CAL-034 bounding basis (615 m³/d, 52 t/d solids, 40.5 t/d lime) — not re-balanced after the V224 cake wash, the spare being margin for M2 / M3. The reactors run as a gravity cascade, so the stage-transfer pumps P-1006 / P-1007 / P-1008 are retired; P-1009A/B is re-purposed as the 18 m³/h underflow pumps (7.3 m³/h to DC-1001 plus the 7.7 m³/h HDS recycle), retiring the bypass pump P-1010; lime to pH 9.8–10 needs no acid trim, retiring T-1004 / P-1001 (no chloride added). Centrate (5.0 m³/h) returns through T-1008 (12 m³; draft 10) and P-1012A/B (6 m³/h) to the CL-1001 feedwell; the 87 t/d of cake (62 m³/d) goes to two covered 40 m³ roll-off containers, each filling in ≈ 15 h (≈ 1.6 swaps a day; the draft said one a day); a new 200 m³ hydrated-lime silo SL-1001 holds two days (draft 180 m³); M-1001 / T-1005 makes down ≈ 264 kg/d of polymer. The BaCl₂ stage is priced as an option for a 1,000 mg/L sulphate limit: ≈ 640 kg/d BaCl₂ and 717 kg/d BaSO₄, R-1003 16 m³ (draft 15), T-1003 30 m³ (4 days), P-1002A/B 0.4 m³/h. With V223, ten A-1000 register tags are now retired; the model still shows them. 20 missing-value gaps close.
findings.action: Obtain the sewer sulphate limit (decides the BaCl₂ option); set the cascade elevations in the A-1000 layout; run settling, dewatering and polymer tests; classify the sludge; raise the PFD-1000 MoC and LST-001 entries (SL-1001, retirements); remove the retired tags from the model; re-balance CAL-034 / -035 when M2 / M3 settle.

findings.topic: PK-1101 V1.2 — stage 1 on MVR, stage 2 on A-5400 steam (A-5000 decision D-A5000-02)
findings.status: DAT-109 / CAL-033 V1.2 issued as candidates; MVR gated on the vendor enquiry (M5)
findings.reason: A1000-07 left the concentrator heat on the A-5400 screen with MVR as the first enquiry question; the A-5000 basis now makes MVR the base case.
findings.observation: Decision D-A5000-02 (A-5000 data layer; bases HS-3 / HS-5 approved in review by QFL 2026-09-27, register V9.1) puts PK-1101 stage 1 — the A-300 stream from 55 to 75 wt %, 34.1 t/d of the 62.8 t/d water evaporated — on mechanical vapour recompression (≈ 0.8 MW electrical) and stage 2 on A-5400 20 barg steam: 1.45 MW normal, 1.65 MW at the 150 t/d rating, 2.0 MW design (was 3.5 MW single-effect). FEED-PE-CAL-033 V1.2 adds the stage split; FEED-PE-DAT-109 V1.2 restates the duty, medium and hold K2. Balance, tanks and pumps are unchanged; the condenser design is kept. The DAT-109 V1.1 rows are superseded in full by the V1.2 rows (existing valueIds unchanged).
findings.action: Ask the concentrator vendors (M5) to confirm MVR on stage 1 at the 55–75 wt % boiling-point elevation; if it is not offered, stage 1 returns to steam and A-5400 needs ≈ 1.5 MW more; add the MVR drive to the electrical load list.

findings.topic: Model catch-up release 1 (D-MDL-01): ten retired tags shown in place; vessels at datasheet volumes
findings.status: Model updated — physical removal with the model engineer
findings.reason: The model still drew the screening A-1000 (100 m³/h basis) and the tags retired by D-A1000-05 / -06.
findings.observation: T-1001, P-1004, T-1007, P-1011 (D-A1000-05) and P-1006, P-1007, P-1008, P-1010, T-1004, P-1001 (D-A1000-06) are kept with their streams, shown grey and labelled RETIRED. T-1006 is now 400 m³ (Ø 8.4 m, FEED-PE-DAT-114), R-1001 25 m³, R-1002 30 m³, R-1004 10 m³, T-1002 80 m³, T-1008 12 m³, and the BaCl₂ option R-1003 16 m³ / T-1003 30 m³; BIN-1001 is labelled as two 40 m³ roll-off containers. Diameters are model choices. The screening calculation and PFD-1000 continuity records are unchanged. CL-1001 and SL-1001 follow in release 2.
findings.action: Model engineer to remove the retired tags and re-route the gravity cascade (docs/model-catchup-handoff.md); release 2 adds CL-1001 and SL-1001.

decisions.rationale: Plant-wide ruling: FEED-PE-MAT-002 'Recommended MOC (base case)' governs material of construction over FEED-PE-MDL-001 (scale-up study) and design-note wording — MAT-002 is the controlled MoC matrix and postdates MDL-001. Wording variants of the same material family are superseded by the MAT-002 statement.
decisions.gapNote: MAT-002 does not cover 2 item(s) with an MDL-001 material only (M-1001, T-1005): extend MAT-002 before those MoCs are approved.

decisions.rationale: REP-038 first-principles load adopted as the design statement: 0.64 mol/L H₂SO₄ + 0.23 mol/L HCl (179 t/d H₂SO₄, 24 t/d HCl) with Mn / K / P — the feed is dilute acid, not wastewater.
decisions.gapNote: Decide the A-1000 discharge route and the spent-acid recovery case (REP-039: 150–200 t/d reconcentration; MOC-001 Part D.1) before any A-1000 / A-2000 sizing; then issue the first A-1000 / A-2000 stream tables (none exist) on DBM V2.0 with the wastewater range by case (REP-038).

decisions.rationale: 2,850 m³/d as drawn vs 400–600 m³/d with acid recovery vs DBM 30–75 m³/d (corrected by MOC-001 to a range by case): no flow approved until the acid-recovery decision.
Acid recovery is the governing design lever for A-1000 / A-2000 (REP-026 F-39, REP-039); A-1000 not to be frozen before it.
NaOH rapid stage to pH 3–4 is not viable at 0.64 mol/L (≈ 166 t/d NaOH; sulphate stays soluble; RO unworkable) — lime-first flowsheet adopted as intent; PFD-1000 R-1001 duty to be redefined by MoC.
decisions.gapNote: MoC on FEED-PFD-1000: remove the NaOH rapid-neutralisation stage or re-purpose R-1001 (lime / limestone-then-lime high-density-sludge); restate reagent tanks T-1001 / T-1002 and dosing pumps accordingly.

decisions.rationale: Lime stage stoichiometry (≈ 149 t/d Ca(OH)₂, 314 t/d gypsum, Case 0) adopted as the chemistry basis; quantities scale with the acid-recovery case.
BaCl₂ polishing conditional on the local sewer sulphate limit vs gypsum saturation (≈ 1,480 mg/L).
≈ 2 MW neutralisation heat (REP-026 F-42) is deleted under acid recovery — duty follows D-A1000-01.
Sludge rate (≈ 340 t/d Case 0) follows the acid-recovery case.

Spent-acid recovery (REP-039 Route 2 + 6) is the FEED base case for the wet train, gated on M1 (filterability at 50–60 wt %), M2 (recycled-acid quality) and M3 (Mn(VII) = 0 before heating); Route 0 (neutralise) stays as the fallback envelope. Answers the acid-recovery decision D-A1000-01 left open. Applied first to A-300 (bases RA1–RA6, FEED-PE-CAL-032 V1.1); A-160 (Route 6), the concentrator package and the residual A-1000 sizing follow.
decisions.gapNote: Tests M1–M3 (REP-039); spent-acid concentrator package (new tag, A-5400 duty); A-160 Route 6 revision (CAL-016); A-1000 sized for the residual

decisions.rationale: Spent-acid concentrator package carried on bases CN1–CN9 as a budget envelope in a new area A-1100: two-stage vacuum concentration of the A-300 filtrate (55 wt %) and the A-160 acid (90 wt %) to 93 wt % — 117.6 t/d H₂SO₄ normal, 140 t/d rated, 115.5 t/d recovered, ≈ 55 t/d water evaporated; 2.26 MW normal / 3.5 MW design heat on A-5400, condensers on A-5200; ≈ 5.8 t/d Mn / K salts purged; Mn(VII) = 0 interlock at T-1101; vent to S1; T-1101 100 m³, T-1102 200 m³ (two-day quality hold), P-1101A/B 7 m³/h, P-1102A/B 10 m³/h. Budget ≈ $15–30 M. Approved in review by QFL 2026-09-26 (FEED-PE-CAL-033).
decisions.gapNote: REP-039 M5 vendor enquiry (stage split, MVR, materials, CAPEX); A-5400 heat supply pending MOC-002 Part F (screen ≈ 17.6–21.8 MW vs 10 MW provision); M2 recycled-acid quality and organics purge; A-3000 S1 load check for the vent; salt-cake classification; MAT-002 A-1100 rows; PFD / LST-001 entries; model area A-1100

decisions.rationale: A-1000 sized for the REP-039 Route 2 + 6 residual on bases RS1–RS9 (FEED-PE-CAL-034): 615 m³/d and 24.3 t/d H₂SO₄ design, HCl bounding at the PFD dose; lime-only HDS (R-1001 pH 5–6, R-1002 pH 9.8–10, R-1004, new thickener CL-1001, DC-1001); Ca(OH)₂ 20.7–40.5 t/d; gypsum 35.8–45.6 t/d; 0.34 MW, no cooler. Route 0 (REP-038) stays the fallback envelope. Approved in review by QFL 2026-09-27.
decisions.gapNote: Sewer sulphate limit (BaCl₂ stage R-1003 held); A-300 phase 2 HCl dose (REP-037 M3); organics bleed (REP-039 M2); A-400 flows (hold H-01); settling / dewatering tests; sludge classification; PFD-1000 MoC and LST-001 (CL-1001, lime silo); phase 2 datasheets

decisions.rationale: Solids basis from the residual balance (RS5): ≈ 52 t/d dry design, cake ≈ 87 t/d at 60 wt %.
Neutralisation heat 0.26–0.34 MW absorbed by the flow; no cooler (RS1).

Retired (RS6 / RS7): NaOH service deleted by the lime-first flowsheet (D-A1000-02); the Pre-G decant receiver and lift pump have no service after A-160 Option B / Route 6. Model geometry to be removed.

A-1000 phase 2 on bases P2-1–P2-9 (FEED-PE-CAL-035): gravity cascade R-1001 → R-1002 → R-1003 → R-1004 → CL-1001 retires the stage-transfer pumps P-1006 / P-1007 / P-1008; P-1009A/B re-purposed as the 18 m³/h underflow pumps (DC-1001 feed + HDS recycle) retires the bypass pump P-1010; no acid trim retires T-1004 / P-1001; T-1008 12 m³ / P-1012A/B centrate return; BIN-1001 two 40 m³ roll-off containers; new SL-1001 200 m³ lime silo; M-1001 / T-1005 polymer make-down; BaCl₂ stage R-1003 16 m³ / T-1003 30 m³ / P-1002A/B carried as a priced option (1,000 mg/L). Sized on the CAL-034 bounding basis, not re-balanced. Approved in review by QFL 2026-09-27.

0.64 mol/L H₂SO₄ + 0.23 mol/L HCl: 179 t/d H₂SO₄, 24 t/d HCl, 129 kmol/d H₃PO₄; 1,070 mg/L Mn, 760 mg/L K, 1,400 mg/L P — dilute acid, not wastewater

NaOH 'rapid' stage to pH 3–4 is not viable at 0.64 mol/L: ≈ 166 t/d NaOH (≈ $22 M/y), sulphate stays soluble as Na₂SO₄, doubles gypsum solubility, makes RO unworkable — NaOH has no place upstream of lime

Lime stage to pH 8.5–10.5: ≈ 149 t/d Ca(OH)₂; 314 t/d gypsum + 20 t/d Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 5 t/d Mn(OH)₂ (≈ 100 kt/y sludge, 500 kg per kg product); DBM A-2 (46 kt/y lime, 98 kt/y sludge) confirmed within 10 %
BaCl₂ sulphate polishing only where the local sewer sulphate limit is below gypsum saturation (≈ 1,480 mg/L); barium $2–4 M/y if required

Acid recovery (150–200 t/d spent-acid reconcentration, 1.5–4.4 MW at 150–200 °C) removes ≈ 95 % of the A-1000 load — 'largest single design lever in the project' (REP-026 F-39); A-1000/A-2000 not to be frozen before the recovery decision

Spent-acid recovery, REP-039 Route 2 + 6: TLGO separated from 50–60 wt % acid in A-300 (Route 2) and the GIC from the A-160 acid before washing (Route 6); the filtrates are reconcentrated and recycled, so A-1000 treats only the residual (≈ 6–15 t/d acid). Gated on M1 (filterability at 50–60 wt %), M2 (recycled-acid quality) and M3 (Mn(VII) = 0 before heating); Route 0 (neutralise everything in A-1000) is the fallback

Two-stage vacuum reconcentration of the Route 2 + 6 spent acid to 93 wt % (REP-039 §3, §9): 117.6 t/d H₂SO₄ normal, 140 t/d rated, ≈ 55 t/d water evaporated, 3.5 MW design heat on A-5400 (MVR option), Mn / K salt separator, Mn(VII) interlock at T-1101; budget envelope gated on the M5 vendor enquiry
Route 2 + 6 residual: 615 m³/d design (25.6 m³/h), ≈ 495 m³/d normal; 24.3 t/d H₂SO₄ design (18.6 firm + 5.8 organics-bleed allowance), HCl 3 t/d (M3) to 18.2 t/d (PFD dose, bounding)
